claim: The bare ありません front has two meanings the learner knows (there isn't / do not have) and the card accepts only 'Do not have', while its base card arimasu-have carries a hint that this conjugated form lacks.
evidence: Recognition front: 'ありません' with no hint; back 'Answer: Do not have'. Lesson 12 taught あります as 'Be, exist' and なにもありません as 'There is nothing'; arimasu-have's front adds 'about owning something'.
fix: Add the same hint as arimasu-have ('about owning something') to the Recognition face.
verdictReason: No earlier standalone ありません card exists (ledger has only じゃありません), so there is no target collision; arimasu-have carries its hint because Lesson 12 has a bare あります card. 'There isn't' and 'do not have' are the same word, and this card's note itself says it negates 'there is / have', so neither reading is a wrong answer.

claim: The bare ありました front reads as 'there was' to a learner who met it in Lesson 13, but the card wants 'Had', and nothing on the front says possession.
evidence: Recognition front: 'ありました' with no hint; back 'Answer: Had'. Ledger: えんぴつはつくえのうえにありました 'The pencil was on the desk.', きょねんえきのまえにコンビニがありました 'Last year there was a convenience store in front of the station.'
fix: Add the hint 'about owning something', matching arimasu-have.
verdictReason: No earlier standalone ありました card exists (the Lesson 13 forms are inside sentences), so no collision. 'There was' and 'had' are one word; a learner reading it either way has understood it. The hint on arimasu-have is there to split it from Lesson 12's bare あります card, which has no counterpart here.

claim: The bare ありませんでした front reads as 'there wasn't' from Lesson 12-13, but the card wants 'Did not have', with no hint.
evidence: Recognition front: 'ありませんでした'; back 'Answer: Did not have'. Ledger: きょねんえきのまえにコンビニがありませんでした 'Last year there was no convenience store in front of the station.'
fix: Add the hint 'about owning something', matching arimasu-have.
verdictReason: Same as arimasen and arimashita: no earlier standalone ありませんでした card, one word for both senses, and the note on this card already contrasts it with じゃありませんでした. Not a wrong answer either way.

claim: The note says again what the front's hint already says.
evidence: Hint on both fronts: 'used to confirm an offer that seems too generous or unexpected'. Note: 'Said when someone makes an unexpected offer, to check they really mean it.'
fix: Drop the note, or use it for something new, such as a typical reply or what the ん in いいんですか is doing.
verdictReason: Hint 'used to confirm an offer that seems too generous or unexpected' and note 'Said when someone makes an unexpected offer, to check they really mean it' say the same thing. card-rules-shared.md: a note must never restate the card.

claim: The note sends the learner to 'GRAMMAR 1–2', a section of a book the learner does not have in Anki.
evidence: Note: 'Marks the giver with もらいます (moraimasu, 'receive from'); with あげます (agemasu) the same に (ni) marks the receiver instead — see GRAMMAR 1–2.'
fix: Remove the 'see GRAMMAR 1–2' pointer; the note already says what it needs to.
verdictReason: Note ends 'see GRAMMAR 1–2', a pointer into the book's page the learner does not have in Anki. The sentence before it already states the rule, so the pointer can go.

claim: The note says 'Compare with the previous card', but in a shuffled deck there is no previous card.
evidence: Note: 'Compare with the previous card: あげました (agemashita) and もらいました (moraimashita) describe the same event from the giver's and receiver's side'.
fix: Name the card it means, e.g. 'Compare スミスさんはなかむらさんにはなをあげました'.
verdictReason: Note says 'Compare with the previous card'; the card meant is ks1-ageru-hana (スミスさんはなかむらさんにはなをあげました), and cards are shuffled. The chapter's other mirror pairs name their twin in full, so this is the odd one out.

claim: 'A friend gave me a scarf.' accepts マフラー as well as スカーフ, because マフラー is glossed 'Muffler, scarf'.
evidence: Production front: 'A friend gave me a scarf.' (answer ともだちがわたしにスカーフをくれました). mafuraa: 'Muffler, scarf', note 'both mean the same thing'.
fix: Fixed by narrowing the マフラー gloss (see the scarf finding); no change to this card needed beyond that.
verdictReason: True as stated: with マフラー glossed 'Muffler, scarf' and its note equating the two, 'A friend gave me a scarf.' admits マフラー. No edit on this card; it clears when the mafuraa finding is fixed.

claim: The note only glosses the two parts of the phrase, both of which the learner already has on earlier cards.
evidence: Note: 'おみやげ (omiyage) means souvenir/gift; きょうと (Kyouto) is the city Kyoto.' Ledger: おみやげ 'Souvenir' (Lesson 11), きょうと 'Kyoto' (Lesson 6).
fix: Drop the note.
verdictReason: Ledger: きょうと 'Kyoto' (Lesson 6), おみやげ 'Souvenir' (Lesson 11). The note only glosses the two parts, both already known. Dropping it also removes the 'Kyouto' romaji preflight flags against the deck's own 'kyōto'.

claim: The romaji writes the long vowel as 'mafuraa', while the word's own card writes 'mafurā'.
evidence: Back: 'Says: Suteki na mafuraa desu ne'. Card mafuraa: 'Says: mafurā'.
fix: Write 'mafurā' here so the romaji matches the vocabulary card.
verdictReason: cards.json pronunciation 'Suteki na mafuraa desu ne' against mafuraa's 'mafurā'. card-authoring-rules.md pins macrons for long vowels, never doubled vowels. Preflight's long-vowel-macron lint caught the two 'ou' cases in this unit but not this 'aa', so it is not already reported.

claim: The note says only four colour words are い-adjectives, but the learner has two more on earlier cards, ちゃいろい and きいろい.
evidence: Note: 'くろい (kuroi) is a true い-adjective, so の never appears here. Same for あかい (akai), あおい (aoi) and しろい (shiroi) — those four and no others.' Ledger, Lesson 5 extras: ちゃいろい 'Brown', きいろい 'Yellow', これはきいろいかさです 'This is a yellow umbrella.'; Lesson 12 extras: これはちゃいろいつくえです 'This is a brown desk.'
fix: Drop 'those four and no others', or say that ちゃいろい and きいろい work the same way while みどり, ピンク and the others take の.
verdictReason: Ledger has ちゃいろい 'Brown' and きいろい 'Yellow' (Lesson 5 extras) plus これはきいろいかさです and これはちゃいろいつくえです, so 'those four and no others' is false and contradicts cards the learner already holds. Teaches something false, so blocker. Both roles found it; merged.

claim: With no owner named and no scene, a learner reads スカーフがありますよ as 'there's a scarf' (Lesson 12), not 'I have a scarf'.
evidence: Recognition front: 'あ、スカーフがありますよ' with no hint; back 'Oh, I have a scarf.' Every other 'have' card names the owner with は (わたしはくるまがあります, わたしはおかねがありません). The note also says 'The chapter's first use of あります as "have"', which means nothing in a shuffle.
fix: Add a scene such as 'offering a scarf to someone who says it is cold', and drop 'the chapter's first use' from the note.
verdictReason: The line and its English are the TARGET DIALOGUE verbatim ('Oh, I have a scarf.'), and 'there's a scarf' is the same utterance, so the card is faithful and answerable; downgraded to polish. Still true that no scene carries the book's context (Nakamura pulls a scarf from her bag to offer it) and that 'The chapter's first use' is an ordering claim that means nothing in a shuffle.

claim: 'It's a lovely bag' fits かばん (taught since Lesson 2) as well as バッグ, and the hint does not choose.
evidence: Production front: 'It's a lovely bag, isn't it? Where did you buy it? / complimenting something a friend is carrying' (answer すてきなバッグですね…). Ledger: かばん 'Bag'. Card baggu tells them apart only with its own hint 'a fashion bag like a purse or tote (loanword)'.
fix: Add 'handbag' or 'purse' to the English, or a hint like 'the loanword for a fashion bag'.
verdictReason: Ledger has かばん 'Bag' (Lesson 2) and ふくろ 'Bag' (Lesson 5); すてきなかばんですね is correct Japanese, so nothing on the front picks バッグ. The deck's own baggu card needed the hint 'a fashion bag like a purse or tote (loanword)' for the same collision; this authored sentence needs the same cue.

claim: The English says 'evening', which the learner has as ばん, but the answer uses よる, which this chapter glosses 'Night'.
evidence: Production front: 'Do you have time tomorrow evening?' (answer あしたのよるじかんがありますか). Ledger: ばん 'Evening' (Lesson 3), まいばん 'Every evening'. Card yoru: 'Night'. fib-kinyoubi-isogashii-q renders きんようびのよる as 'Friday night'.
fix: Change the English to 'Do you have time tomorrow night?'.
verdictReason: Ledger: ばん 'Evening' (Lesson 3), まいばん 'Every evening'; this chapter's yoru card says 'Night' and fib-kinyoubi-isogashii-q renders きんようびのよる as 'Friday night'. あしたのばん would also be correct, so 'tomorrow evening' does not determine よる. The card is deck-authored (the book's task says only 'ask if they have time tomorrow evening'), so its English is free to change to 'tomorrow night'.

claim: The note rules out だれから, which looks like it should work given から 'From', and nothing taught says it is wrong.
evidence: Note: 'だれに, not だれから — with もらいます the giver is marked by に.' Ledger: から 'From (particle)' (Lesson 3).
fix: Say that に is the form this lesson uses for the giver, without calling から wrong (or, if から is accepted, say both work).
verdictReason: Book GRAMMAR 2 says に means 'from' with もらいます and never calls から wrong. だれからもらいましたか is ordinary Japanese (もらう takes に or から for the giver), so the note's prohibition is both unverifiable from the deck and false as stated. Say に is the form this lesson uses.

claim: A learner who has just read that a gift to 'my colleague' takes くれます cannot tell why どうりょう here takes あげます.
evidence: Front: 'どうりょうにあげます / answering who Emma-san will give the ring to'; back '(She) will give it to a colleague.' x14b-tsuma-iyaringu-kuremashita note: 'A gift to my wife, my family or my colleague still counts as coming towards me, so it is くれました and not あげました.' Ledger: どうりょう 'Colleague, coworker'.
fix: Make the English 'to her colleague' so the in-group rule visibly does not apply, or add that line to the note.
verdictReason: The card is correct: Emma-san is a third party, so あげます is right and the tsuma-card note about 'my colleague' does not apply. Whether a learner conflates the two is a judgement I cannot settle from the cards; 'to her colleague' would remove the doubt at no cost, so worth doing if the fixer is in the file.

claim: 'It's a lovely scarf, isn't it?' can be answered with マフラー, because the deck glosses マフラー 'Muffler, scarf' and its twin card says the same sentence with マフラー.
evidence: Production front: 'It's a lovely scarf, isn't it?' (answer すてきなスカーフですね). Base fib-suteki-mafuraa: 'It's a lovely muffler, isn't it?' → すてきなマフラーですね. mafuraa: 'Muffler, scarf'.
fix: Fixed by narrowing the マフラー gloss (see chapter-14 scarf finding).
verdictReason: True as stated: the twin fib-suteki-mafuraa says the same frame with マフラー, and mafuraa is glossed 'Muffler, scarf'. No edit on this card; it clears when the mafuraa finding is fixed.

claim: The chapter writes the same past negative two ways in romaji, as one word in the base unit and split in the extras.
evidence: Extras: 'kashimasen deshita', 'karimasen deshita', 'agemasen deshita', 'arimasen deshita', 'dōmo sumimasen deshita'. Base: 'kashimasendeshita', 'karimasendeshita', 'agemasendeshita', 'arimasendeshita', 'sumimasendeshita'.
fix: Pick one spacing for -masen deshita and use it across both units.
verdictReason: cards.json pronunciation: base unit writes all seven -masendeshita as one word; extras splits five ('kashimasen deshita', 'karimasen deshita', 'agemasen deshita', 'dōmo sumimasen deshita', 'arimasen deshita') and leaves one joined ('sengetsu yakusoku ga arimasendeshita'), so the extras unit is inconsistent even with itself. Collection-wide 37 split vs 21 joined. Preflight's romaji lint does not cover this spacing.

claim: The mafuraa note says マフラー and スカーフ mean the same thing. The book glosses and draws them as two different items, and the shared gloss makes 'Scarf' on the scarf card's Production front (and the scarf sentence fronts) fit two words.
evidence: Book, WORD POWER Gifts picture (Page_133_Image_0003): ④ スカーフ is a patterned neck scarf on the woman, ⑨ マフラー a thick knitted winter scarf on the man; VOCABULARY: 'スカーフ scarf', 'マフラー muffler, scarf'. Card mafuraa: English 'Muffler, scarf', note 'A second word for scarf, alongside スカーフ (sukaafu) — both mean the same thing.' Card scarf Production front: 'Clothing / Scarf' (answer スカーフ). Same split on kuremasu-example and x14-suteki-na-sukaafu-desune.
fix: Gloss マフラー as 'Muffler (a thick winter scarf)' and rewrite the note to contrast it with スカーフ, a light decorative scarf, instead of equating them; then 'scarf' on a front means スカーフ alone.
verdictReason: Checked the gifts picture and VOCABULARY: the book draws and glosses two different items. 'Both mean the same thing' is the deck's own addition, and it is what makes the three 'scarf' Production fronts fit two words. Same root problem seen from both sides, so merged.

claim: The note calls から a suffix, while the book (and the card's own English) call it a particle.
evidence: Book, VOCABULARY: "から because (particle; see NOTES 2)"; NOTES 2: "から is added after an explanatory phrase, signaling a reason for something." Card English: "Because (particle)"; note: "Suffix — attaches after an explanatory clause to give a reason (clause + から (kara))."
fix: Replace "Suffix" with "Particle".
verdictReason: Book VOCABULARY: 'から because (particle; see NOTES 2)'; card English 'Because (particle)'; note opens 'Suffix —'. Preflight's note-claims tier only flags that the note asserts a composition, it does not judge the word, so not already reported.

claim: The scene cue says よく is "about how skillfully", but the book teaches it only as the "well" of よく にあいますね (it suits you well), which the card's own note also says.
evidence: Book, EXERCISES VIII VOCABULARY: "よく にあいますね。 It suits you well." / "よく well". Card scene: "about how skillfully"; card note: "here it's the manner adverb 'well,' as in よく にあいますね".
fix: Change the scene to something like "how well something suits someone".
verdictReason: Book, EXERCISES VIII VOCABULARY: the only よく in this chapter is よく にあいますね 'It suits you well', which the card's own note cites. 'About how skillfully' is the deck's cue and misdescribes it; the cue still has to separate this card from Lesson 9's よく 'Often', so reword rather than drop. Both roles found it; merged.

claim: The scene says the line answers about Smith-san's father giving him money, but くれます here (and the English "gives it to me") only works if the speaker is the receiver; its paired question asks about the asker's own father giving the asker money, so the pair does not fit together.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 1 NOTE: "あげます cannot be used in a sentence meaning 'someone gives something to me (the speaker)'; in that case the verb くれます is used." Card: たんじょうびにくれます, scene "answering when Smith-san's father gives him money", English "(He) gives it to me for my birthday." Paired question fib-chichi-itsu-okane-kuremasu-q: ちちはいつわたしにおかねをくれますか "When does (my) father give me money?"
fix: Make the scene "Smith-san answering when his father gives him money" and rewrite the question to ask Smith about his father (e.g. スミスさん、おとうさんは いつ おかねを くれますか).
verdictReason: Checked both faces. The question card is phrased from the speaker's own side (ちち, わたしに), so nobody else can ask it, while the answer card's scene says it answers about Smith-san's father. The cast of the pair does not line up. Both roles found it on opposite halves of the pair; merged, kept on the answer card since the fix rewrites the question to match it.
